title: Bound committed-slice recovery and same-slice marker scans to the fixed WK fork

criteria: Committed-slice integration must not inspect commits before the launcher-owned fixed WK fork when answering the pre-admission zero-delta recovery question or authenticating same-slice marker history for advanceSliceRefCas. The fixed lifecycle floor is the exact direct commit at refs/agent-launch/wk-forks/<IN>/<WK>, derived only from validated canonical initiative/WK identity. Current main, merge-base, caller input, prompt, environment, record prose/status, reviewer output, and arbitrary reachability carry no floor authority.

Bounding must preserve exact zero-delta evidence cardinality and binding semantics, exact-current corrective-delivery marker matching, literal parent/object/message authentication, current-tip versus historical evidence distinctions, expected-old ref CAS behavior, record-CAS retry behavior, and all existing fail-closed outcomes.

No history proof or cache may cross a ref movement, record-CAS retry, or other observation boundary that invalidates its exact WK-tip/fork binding. The design must state whether and how one bounded authenticated post-fork observation can serve both recovery and fresh integration without weakening re-observation requirements.

Disposition requests that are structurally invalid or cannot match retained exact-target findings must be rejected before avoidable expensive history traversal, while exact-target evidence matching remains server-derived and cannot be selected by caller-carried authority.
The generic MCP oversized-response spill and integration-result evidence projection are out of scope for this WK; this WK owns the two whole-history integration scans only.

Before implementation dispatch, author and mechanically assess the controlled acceptance contract, map every operative obligation and named validation scenario to its implementation mechanism and proof coverage, and complete the required DRY-violation review. Preserve any unresolved authority or reuse question as a blocker rather than guessing.
validation: Real-Git regression with at least 500 pre-fork commits and representative post-fork ordinary, corrective, and zero-delta integration commits; instrument subprocess/object reads and prove neither target path reads a pre-fork commit.

Reproduce a valid non-final workspace_integrate_committed_slice success and an invalid-disposition refusal. Prove cost is independent of pre-fork history size, invalid disposition avoids the unnecessary history scans, and the successful path does not perform two independent full-root walks.

Exercise zero, one, and multiple exact zero-delta matches; current-tip and historical evidence; singular and plural same-slice corrective markers; malformed claims; wrong delivery/base/WK-parent; merge paths; cycles; missing objects; bound exhaustion; fork absence/movement/deletion; and concurrent WK-ref and record-CAS races.
